comment: What `feint corpus --check` knows about the committed corpora: when each was
recorded, and which divergences from the real cloud this repository records
rather than fails on. Modelled on tools/compat/accepted.json, including the
rule that gives that file its teeth: an entry that excuses nothing fails the
gate, because a stale exemption is a gate that quietly stopped covering what
it names. Every accepted divergence is still printed, with its reason, on
every run.
THE LIST WENT FROM EMPTY TO FOUR ENTRIES FOR THREE FIELDS, AND THAT IS THE
CHAIN WORKING. It went in empty because #355 had deleted the eight
divergences #352 recorded: the staleness rule made the deletion compulsory,
since an entry that excuses nothing fails the gate. Those eight had three
causes, and saying which was the work:
THE LIST WAS EMPTY UNTIL A BILLED RESOURCE WAS RECORDED, AND THAT IS THE
WHOLE STORY OF THIS FILE. The gate went in carrying the eight divergences
#352's first recording found; #355 retired all eight, and the staleness rule
made their deletion compulsory the day the emulator stopped producing them.
The list then sat empty for one reason nobody had written down: the corpus
held nothing billed. A VPC, a private network and an SSH key are free, so
the two recordings covered exactly the operations that cost nothing — and
every ReplayInvariant this repository declares lives on CreateServer,
GetServer and UpdateServer. values_checked was 0 and orders_checked was 0,
including for the order of Server.public_ips, which is #320, a defect that
cost a pull request and that nothing in this repository was exercising.
So one DEV1-S and one flexible IP were created on a real account in fr-par,
with the owner's explicit and bounded consent, and destroyed three seconds
later (`corpus/scaleway/scw-instance.jsonl`, recorded 2026-08-21, alive from
17:32:27 to 17:32:30 +02:00, every destruction proved by a read answering
404 and the starting and final inventories identical family by family).
That single recording moved values_checked to 2 and orders_checked to 6, and
surfaced the twenty-six divergences below.
THE FOUR EXOSCALE ENTRIES ARE GONE, AND THAT IS THE RULE ABOVE DOING ITS
WORK. The #354 recording surfaced four divergences of one kind — a field the
cloud answers that this emulator omitted — and getting to see them at all
took fixing the instrument first: three sanitiser defects buried them, all
measured on the same file and all falsified in
tools/falsify/specs/sanitised-corpus.json:
- `0.0.0.0/0` cannot be replaced: masking a zero-length prefix yields the
same prefix, so the cross-reference found it in the recording and in the
artefact and refused to write anything. Every security-group rule that
opens a port to the internet carries it.
- `255.255.255.0` went through the address mint and came out a host
address, so `create-private-network` answered 400 `netmask is not a
usable IPv4 netmask` where the cloud answered 200.
- `start-ip` and `end-ip` were minted in the order the walk met them, so
the range ran backwards and the same create answered 400 `end-ip is
below start-ip`. Together those two hid the whole private-network
lifecycle behind about twenty findings, not one of them the emulator's.
What was left after that was three fields across four entries — zones[].id
(51 findings), security-groups[].visibility on the list (44) and on the get
(2), and rules[].security-group.name (8) — and #370 and #371 retired all
four. Their shared root is worth keeping written down, because it is the one
no document-reading control could ever have found: the cloud answers fields
its own published API description does not declare, so the contract, the
shapes gate, the probe and the pack all agreed with each other and all four
were wrong the same way. Two of the three now live in
tools/contract/exoscale-recorded-fields.yaml, which folds a field into the
contract only with the recording that proves it and is held to that recording
by internal/cli's TestEveryRecordedFieldIsStillOnTheWire — the same staleness
rule as this list, pointed the other way: a citation that cites nothing is as
dead as an exemption that excuses nothing. The third needed no contract
change at all; the document already declared the field and only the pack had
dropped it.
An empty list is not a licence. The next divergence a recording surfaces
goes here with its reason and the issue that retires it, or the gate stays
red — and a corpus trimmed until it passes is the one outcome this file
exists to make impossible.
THEY ARE CLASSIFIED AND NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY. Classifying a divergence
and correcting it are two pieces of work, and doing them in one pass is how
a classification becomes whatever the patch happened to make green. Each
entry therefore names the issue that deletes it, and the staleness rule
above makes that deletion compulsory rather than polite. Five causes:
- #365, the root volume. The cloud gave the DEV1-S an SBS volume and scw
read it through block/v1alpha1; this emulator gives a local instance/v1
volume, so the read and the delete answer 404. Sixteen entries, and the
fourteen absent fields are the body of an object that is simply not
there — one wildcard entry rather than fourteen, because they have one
cause and would be retired by one change.
- #366, two keys the cloud writes and this emulator omits: bootscript
(null) and extra_networks ([]). Untriaged, which is the point of the
issue: they are either served or declared in DeclinedFields(), and a
corpus exemption is neither.
- #367, image.from_server is an empty string on the wire and null here.
- #368, an attached public IP publishes no gateway and drops its own tags,
in public_ip and in every element of public_ips.
- #369, createServer honours a project the request names and listServers
scopes an unfiltered list to the default project, so the list answers
zero where the cloud answered one. The create and the list disagree
about which project the caller is in.
None of the five is an artefact of the instrument, which is worth saying
because the first recording's eight were mostly that: two were the replay
grading data-keyed maps as fields and five were the proxy's own redaction
destroying public_key. #355 fixed the instrument, and what this recording
surfaced is the emulator and the cloud disagreeing.
ONE OF THE THREE FILES WAS RECORDED AGAINST NO ACCOUNT AT ALL, and it is
worth saying why that is a measurement rather than a shortcut.
outscale/oapi-cli-catalogue.jsonl was driven with the public placeholder
credentials of tools/conformance/outscale/fake-credentials.env, in a config
file holding exactly one profile named on the command line. Measured on
2026-08-21 against api.eu-west-2.outscale.com: five operations answer 200
to an unknown access key — ReadRegions, ReadVmTypes, ReadPublicIpRanges,
ReadPublicCatalog, ReadFlexibleGpuCatalog — and every authenticated one
answers 400 InvalidParameterValue 4120. So the provider's own catalogue is
recordable by anyone, from any station, with no account to put at risk and
no inventory in the answers, and this is the first time this repository has
compared its Outscale pack with the real cloud rather than with a document.
THE TWENTY-FIVE OUTSCALE ENTRIES COME FROM THE FIRST RECORDING OF A REAL
OUTSCALE ACCOUNT (#354), and the same sentence applies to them as to the
Scaleway ones: they are classified and not fixed, deliberately. That
recording is also the reason this file can say anything about an Outscale
value or an Outscale order at all — the pack declared no ReplayInvariant
until #354, so `feint corpus --check` had been printing "0 divergent
finding(s)" over a run in which no value and no order of an Outscale answer
was ever compared. values_checked and orders_checked went from 2 and 6, all
of them Scaleway's, to 5 and 56. Seven causes:
- #378, a Vm answers no UserData, no BlockDeviceMappings and no Tags. The
middle one is the one with teeth: it is where a client reads the root
volume it must not delete, the same gap #365 records on Scaleway.
- #379, the order of a machine's security groups is the reverse of the
cloud's, on the update and on the reads after it. #320 one provider out,
and the very first order this repository has compared against a real
Outscale answer. It also settles that the cloud does NOT answer the
order the client named: the request said web-then-db and the cloud said
db-then-web, so the invariant holds the emulator to the cloud's order.
- #380, a delete is instantaneous here and asynchronous upstream, so every
read of the teardown answers a terminal-state object there and nothing
here — and a security group a just-terminated machine still holds is
refused 409 for two minutes upstream and accepted at once here.
- #381, DeleteRoute and DeleteLoadBalancer answer no body.
- #382, a rule whose source is another group omits that group's AccountId.
- #383, the emulated image catalogue's entries carry neither their device
mapping nor their launch permissions.
- #384 IS NOT THE EMULATOR. The recorder replaces the value under
KeypairName, because the name carries `key`, so the real keypair's name
and the invented one of a deliberate refusal both became "REDACTED" and
the transcript says two objects were one. It is filed against the
instrument and its entries are not the emulator's debt.
FOUR DEFECTS OF THE INSTRUMENT HAD TO GO FIRST, AGAIN, and between them they
hid the whole lifecycle behind about a hundred findings: the Outscale pack
vouched for none of the closed lists it validates a request against (so the
subregion, the flow of a rule, the kind of a load balancer and the protocol
of a listener all became synthetic strings and every create carrying one
answered 400); the sanitiser minted each CIDR independently, so a Subnet
landed outside its Net; the gate replayed every corpus against one region,
so a cloudgouv recording met a pack publishing eu-west-2's zones; and #384.
The first three are fixed and falsified in tools/falsify/specs/.
HOW A CORPUS AGES. `warn_after_days` warns and never fails. This gate holds
one side of the comparison — it can say the emulator and the recording
disagree, and nothing in it knows which of the two moved. Failing on age
would be asserting exactly what it cannot measure, and a gate that fails
because the cloud changed is a gate somebody disables. #359 is the half that
can arbitrate: it replays the corpus against the cloud. Until then the
warning names the file, its age and the re-recording procedure
(corpus/README.md), and 180 days is a chosen horizon rather than a measured
one: about two releases, and short enough that a Scaleway surface which
gained 453 SDK methods in twelve months has not silently outrun the file.

accepted.reason: A real machine is born with a root BSU volume, and this emulator's machines model none (docs/limits.md), so the device mapping is an empty list where the cloud answers the root device with its volume, its link date and DeleteOnVmDeletion. It is where a client reads the root volume it must not delete, and the same gap #365 records on the Scaleway side. The other two fields of #378 are served since 2026-08-21; this one is left because giving every machine a volume changes a limit this repository declared on purpose rather than an oversight, and that is the owner's decision to take.

The cloud refuses DeleteSecurityGroup with 409 ResourceConflict for about ninety seconds after the machine that wore the group is terminated, and accepts on the thirty-first attempt; this emulator releases the group the moment the machine is terminated and answers 200 at once. A REPLAY CANNOT GRADE THE DIFFERENCE EITHER WAY: the recording is thirty refusals then an acceptance, and a corpus has no ninety seconds in it, since the sanitiser normalises every timestamp to one second apart. Reproducing the delay would make every stack teardown and every conformance run wait it out, which is a product decision rather than a defect to patch. #380 carries it, and internal/providers/outscale/securitygroups.go records the measurement where the skip is.

The fixed catalogue answers an empty device mapping where the cloud answers the root device with its size and type. Filling it was tried and measured: no state of the pack then satisfies shapes:check, tools/conformance/score.sh and tools/conformance/outscale/terraform.sh at once, because a field decline is written against an operation and ReadImages answers two kinds of object — the catalogue, and an image a client really cut from a snapshot. Naming a SnapshotId the catalogue does not hold is rule 4, and it is the fiction that killed a conformance run once. #389 backs the catalogue with a snapshot the pack really holds, which is what lets this entry go.

Upstream a destroyed object stays readable in a terminal state (deleting, deleted) and this emulator removes it at once, so every read of the recording's teardown answers one element there and none here. Making a delete asynchronous is a change to the lifecycle of every kind and to what 'nothing left behind' means for every conformance suite, not a line in a handler.

scw deletes the root volume through block/v1alpha1 after deleting the server, and the cloud answers 204 where this emulator answers 404 because the volume it created is an instance/v1 one
the cloud gave the DEV1-S an SBS root volume and answers 200 on the block path scw follows; this emulator attaches a local instance/v1 volume, so the same read answers 404

every top-level field of a body this emulator does not serve at all: the block volume behind the root disk does not exist here, so its fourteen fields are absent for the one reason the status divergence above states
the cloud still writes the retired bootscript key as null and this emulator omits the key, which is a different answer from writing it empty
the cloud answers extra_networks as an empty array and this emulator writes no such key, which a client reading the field distinguishes
the image the server embeds carries the same from_server null where the cloud writes an empty string, because it is the same image view
the cloud publishes the gateway address of a routed public IP and this emulator publishes null, so a guest reading its own route off the answer finds nothing
the tags sent on CreateIP reach the cloud's view of the attached address and this emulator answers an empty list, so the element the recording carries has no counterpart
every element of public_ips carries the same null gateway the singular public_ip carries, because the list and the field render through one function
every element of public_ips drops the address tags the cloud propagates, because the list and the singular field render through one function
the cloud answers from_server as an empty string for an image built from no server, and this emulator answers null, which retypes a field the SDK declares as a value

the read carries the same omission of extra_networks as the create, because both render one server view
